whyWrong: A UPS has a limited battery runtime, so it is a temporary solution rather than a permanent one.
Converting mechanical energy into electrical energy describes a generator, not a UPS.
A UPS supports equipment only for a short time during an interruption and does not replace the main power source.
source: CompTIA Security+ SY0-701 Cert Guide (Heuermann) – Chapter 13: Understanding the Importance of Resilience and Recovery in Security Architecture, Do I Know This Already? Quiz question 8

stem: What is the primary difference between load balancing and clustering in the context of high availability?
options: Load balancing distributes traffic, whereas clustering combines multiple servers into one.
Load balancing is for planned outages, whereas clustering is for unplanned outages.
Load balancing is used in cloud computing, whereas clustering is used in on-premises environments.
Load balancing enhances system availability, whereas clustering focuses on business continuity.
explanation: Load balancing distributes traffic or tasks across several servers so that none is overloaded. Clustering connects several servers so they work together as a single system, which allows seamless failover if one node fails.
whyWrong: Both load balancing and clustering help with planned and unplanned outages, so they are not split this way.
Both load balancing and clustering are used in cloud and on-premises environments.
Both techniques improve availability, so this split does not describe the real difference between them.
source: CompTIA Security+ SY0-701 Cert Guide (Heuermann) – Chapter 13: Understanding the Importance of Resilience and Recovery in Security Architecture, Do I Know This Already? Quiz question 9

stem: A large corporation is setting up a web array, consisting of eight web servers, to sell goods on its e-commerce website. It has been decided that they will purchase F5 load balancers so that their web traffic can be optimized for speedy customer delivery. Which of the following BEST describes why load balancing is useful in this scenario?
options: Load balancing will ensure that only authorized users can gain access to the network
Load balancing will provide redundancy for critical data storage
Load balancing will evenly distribute network traffic to prevent bottlenecks
Load balancing will monitor user activity to identify potential threats
explanation: Load balancing evenly distributes network traffic across the web servers, which prevents bottlenecks and overloads. This keeps performance high and the servers available for customers.
whyWrong: Load balancing allocates resources and does not decide which users are authorized to access the network.
Load balancing can add redundancy for servers, but it does not provide data storage redundancy or directly speed delivery.
Load balancing watches traffic to optimize performance, not to identify threats.
source: CompTIA Security+ SY0-701 Certification Guide, 3rd edition (Neil) – Chapter 13: Explain the importance of resilience and recovery in security architecture, Chapter Review Questions question 1

stem: In a data center, which device provides controlled power distribution to servers and networking equipment, ensuring efficient power management and protection against overloads?
explanation: A managed power distribution unit (PDU) controls how power is distributed to servers and networking equipment in a data center. It gives efficient power management, remote monitoring, and protection against overloads.
whyWrong: A UPS provides backup power for a short time during an outage but does not manage power distribution or prevent overloads.
A generator is a backup source for long outages and does not give fine-grained control over power distribution.
A redundant power supply gives a device a second power source but does not manage distribution to other equipment.
source: CompTIA Security+ SY0-701 Certification Guide, 3rd edition (Neil) – Chapter 13: Explain the importance of resilience and recovery in security architecture, Chapter Review Questions question 10
note: SY0-801 power redundancy lists UPS, RPS, generator, and surge protector but not a managed PDU.

stem: Over the past six months, a company has suffered power failures about once a week. This has affected business operations, and the company is now moving to the cloud. Which of the following cloud features would be beneficial to company operations?
explanation: Geographic dispersion spreads resources across several locations, so a power failure at one location does not stop operations. Cloud providers can run the company's workloads in sites far apart, which gives redundancy against local outages.
whyWrong: Cloud backups protect data but do not keep operations running during ongoing power failures.
Redundant or backup power on the company's site would not affect operations that now run in the cloud.
Reduced cost is a general benefit of cloud migration and does not address the power failures.
source: CompTIA Security+ SY0-701 Certification Guide, 3rd edition (Neil) – Chapter 13: Explain the importance of resilience and recovery in security architecture, Chapter Review Questions question 4
note: SY0-701 geographic dispersion; SY0-801 does not name it, closest is redundancy and high availability.

stem: An organization has a site in a remote location that has been suffering intermittent power outages that last between 3 and 10 seconds. Which of the following should the company implement so that the servers can maintain power for up to 10 seconds to shut down gracefully?
options: An additional power unit on each server
explanation: An uninterruptible power supply provides power from batteries immediately when the main power fails. It covers short outages of a few seconds and gives the servers time to shut down gracefully.
whyWrong: A generator needs time to start, so the servers would lose power during short interruptions.
A managed PDU distributes and manages power but provides no backup power.
An additional power unit in each server still depends on the same failed power source.
source: CompTIA Security+ SY0-701 Certification Guide, 3rd edition (Neil) – Chapter 13: Explain the importance of resilience and recovery in security architecture, Chapter Review Questions question 5

stem: Zhuri wants to ensure that her organization’s datacenter remains online during an extended power outage. What power resilience option is best suited to extended outages?
explanation: Generators are used by organizations that need to handle extended power outages. They are commonly paired with UPS systems, which cover the immediate outage while the generator starts and stabilizes.
whyWrong: Solar power is not a good solution for a datacenter without a large battery system, and it produces nothing at night.
A UPS runs on batteries for minutes rather than hours, so it cannot cover an extended outage alone.
PDUs distribute and control power in a datacenter but do not generate or back up power.
source: CompTIA Security+ Practice Tests: Exam SY0-701 (Seidl) – Chapter 3: Domain 3.0: Security Architecture, Review Questions question 104

stem: Which of the following is not a common concern for extended power outages where generators are providing power to a datacenter they were designed to support during outages?
explanation: Generators are normally sized to the datacenter they support, so capacity is rarely a main concern when they were designed for it. Fuel availability, maintenance during long runs, and physical redundancy so that a second generator can take over during maintenance are all common concerns.
whyWrong: Long outages consume fuel quickly, so keeping enough fuel available is a common concern.
Generators running for long periods need maintenance, so maintenance is a common concern.
A second generator is needed to take over during maintenance in a long outage, so physical redundancy is a common concern.
source: CompTIA Security+ Practice Tests: Exam SY0-701 (Seidl) – Chapter 3: Domain 3.0: Security Architecture, Review Questions question 107

stem: Lisa wants to ensure that her organization’s datacenter can properly handle short power disruptions and temporary undervoltage events. What power resilience solution is best suited to her needs?
explanation: UPS systems are well suited to short power outages and temporary undervoltage events. They sit between the systems and grid power and supply clean, reliable power from their batteries.
whyWrong: Generators take time to start, so they do not cover short disruptions unless a UPS bridges the gap.
PDUs distribute and manage power in a datacenter but do not supply power during a disruption.
Solar power can offset consumption but does not handle sudden disruptions and produces nothing at night.
source: CompTIA Security+ Practice Tests: Exam SY0-701 (Seidl) – Chapter 3: Domain 3.0: Security Architecture, Review Questions question 110

stem: Which of the following best describes replication as a resilience strategy?
options: It makes a complete backup copy of live data that can be restored from media if needed, then journaled changes can be replayed to catch up to the moment of failure.
It creates a continuous copy of live data either asynchronously or synchronously.
It uses a series of snapshots to provide disaster recovery for virtual machines.
It requires high-speed media to keep up with live data.
explanation: Replication keeps an up-to-date copy of live data, either synchronously or asynchronously. It needs storage that can keep up with the rate of change in production, but it does not rely on journaling or snapshots.
whyWrong: Restoring a backup from media and replaying journaled changes describes backup and journaling, not replication.
A series of snapshots for virtual machines describes snapshot-based recovery, not replication.
Replication needs storage fast enough to keep up with changes, but it does not require high-speed media as such.
source: CompTIA Security+ Practice Tests: Exam SY0-701 (Seidl) – Chapter 3: Domain 3.0: Security Architecture, Review Questions question 121
note: SY0-701 replication; SY0-801 does not name it, mapped to redundancy strategies.

stem: Kendra is designing a web application infrastructure and wants to use a load balanced cluster. Which of the following considerations is not directly addressed by using a load balancer?
explanation: Risk transference usually needs a contract or insurance, so a load balancer does not address it. Load balancers help availability by removing failed nodes from the pool, responsiveness by sending load to the least loaded systems, and scalability by letting systems be added or removed transparently.
whyWrong: A load balancer improves availability by automatically removing failed nodes from the pool.
A load balancer improves responsiveness by sending requests to the least loaded systems.
A load balancer improves scalability by letting systems be added to or removed from the pool transparently.
source: CompTIA Security+ Practice Tests: Exam SY0-701 (Seidl) – Chapter 3: Domain 3.0: Security Architecture, Review Questions question 131

stem: Kaito has deployed a system that accepts traffic from web browsers and distributes it to systems based on the number of connections that each server has. He has assigned each server a rating based on how powerful it is. Each time a new request comes in, requests are sent to the system with the lowest number of connections after taking into account the relative rating of each server. What type of load balancing is Kaito using?
explanation: Weighted least connection load balancing sends each new request to the server with the fewest connections, adjusted by a weight that reflects how powerful each server is. Kaito's system uses both the connection count and the server rating, which matches this method.
whyWrong: Source IP hashing uses a hash of the IP addresses to choose a server, so returning sessions reach the same server.
Resource-based load balancing looks at available CPU, memory, and bandwidth rather than connection counts and weights.
Round-robin simply moves through the list of servers in order without looking at connections or weights.
source: CompTIA Security+ Practice Tests: Exam SY0-701 (Seidl) – Chapter 3: Domain 3.0: Security Architecture, Review Questions question 147
note: Load-balancing algorithms are not listed in SY0-801; mapped to load balancing.

stem: John has deployed three servers that all respond as though they’re the same device to provide service he runs. What term best describes this configuration?
explanation: Clustering uses two or more systems that provide a service as though they were a single server. Three servers that all respond as the same device match this description.
whyWrong: Load balancing spreads work across multiple independent systems behind a load balancer rather than making them act as one device.
Fail-open means traffic continues to pass through a network device when it fails, which is not a server configuration.
Fail-closed means a device stops traffic when it fails, which is not a server configuration.
source: CompTIA Security+ Practice Tests: Exam SY0-701 (Seidl) – Chapter 3: Domain 3.0: Security Architecture, Review Questions question 151

stem: Cathy wants to build a high-availability infrastructure for her midsize company’s headquarters building network. Which of the following is not a common element for a high-availability network core?
explanation: Geographic dispersion is unlikely for the network core of a single headquarters building. Redundant devices, backup power, and multiple connectivity options are common parts of a highly available network design.
whyWrong: Redundant routers are a common high-availability element that removes a single point of failure in the core.
Generators are a common high-availability element that keeps the core running during power outages.
Multiple connectivity providers are a common high-availability element that keeps the network online when one provider fails.
source: CompTIA Security+ Practice Tests: Exam SY0-701 (Seidl) – Chapter 3: Domain 3.0: Security Architecture, Review Questions question 159

stem: Devin is building a cloud system and wants to ensure that it can adapt to changes in its workload by provisioning or deprovisioning resources automatically. His goal is to ensure that the environment is not overprovisioned or underprovisioned and that he is efficiently spending money on his infrastructure. What concept describes this?
explanation: Elasticity is a cloud concept that automatically provisions and deprovisions resources to match demand. It keeps the environment from being overprovisioned or underprovisioned, so money is spent efficiently.
whyWrong: Vertical scalability means making a system larger or smaller, but it does not by itself match resources automatically to the workload.
Horizontal scalability means adding or removing systems, but it does not by itself match resources automatically to the workload.
Normalization is a development and data concept that keeps data in a consistent form.
source: CompTIA Security+ Practice Tests: Exam SY0-701 (Seidl) – Chapter 3: Domain 3.0: Security Architecture, Review Questions question 16
note: SY0-701 elasticity; SY0-801 lists autoscaling, which provides it.

stem: Nathaniel wants to improve the fault tolerance of a server in his datacenter. If he wants to ensure that a power outage does not cause the server to lose power, what is the first control he should deploy from the following list?
explanation: An uninterruptible power supply (UPS) should be the first priority. It keeps power flowing during an outage for a short time until an alternate source such as a generator comes online.
whyWrong: A generator alone takes time to start, so the server would lose power before the generator takes over.
Dual power supplies protect against the failure of one supply but do not help when the power source itself fails.
A managed PDU gives remote management and power monitoring but does not prevent power loss in an outage.
source: CompTIA Security+ Practice Tests: Exam SY0-701 (Seidl) – Chapter 3: Domain 3.0: Security Architecture, Review Questions question 17

stem: Jack has deployed a load balancer for his organization. When a new connection is made, the load balancer assigns the connection to the next server in a list, moving through the list over time as it distributes connections. What type of load balancing algorithm is in use?
explanation: A round-robin algorithm assigns each new connection to the next server in a list. It spreads load without knowing how busy each server is and relies on connections evening out over time.
whyWrong: Capacity-based algorithms use knowledge of each server's capacity rather than simply moving through a list.
Least load algorithms send connections to the least busy server rather than to the next server in a list.
User pinning is not a load-balancing algorithm.
source: CompTIA Security+ Practice Tests: Exam SY0-701 (Seidl) – Chapter 3: Domain 3.0: Security Architecture, Review Questions question 187
note: Load-balancing algorithms are not listed in SY0-801; mapped to load balancing.

stem: Danielle’s organization has experienced a total power outage. The datacenter is currently running on its UPS. What concern should Danielle have if the UPS is her organization’s only power resilience control?
options: The UPS batteries may run out before the outage is over.
The generator may run out of fuel in a long outage.
The UPS may not handle the surge when power resumes.
explanation: A UPS runs on batteries and is usually intended to run for minutes, not hours. With no generator or other power control, a long outage can drain the batteries before power returns.
whyWrong: No generator is mentioned, because the UPS is the organization's only power resilience control.
No generator is in use, so running out of generator fuel is not a concern here.
UPS systems are designed to handle power returning after an outage while protecting the systems they power.
source: CompTIA Security+ Practice Tests: Exam SY0-701 (Seidl) – Chapter 3: Domain 3.0: Security Architecture, Review Questions question 190

stem: Liana wants to deploy a load balancer and wants to ensure that if a session is interrupted users have the highest chance of being reconnected to the same server. What algorithm should she select?
explanation: IP hash load balancing uses a hash of the client and server IP addresses to associate a client with a server. Because the same client hashes to the same server, an interrupted session has the best chance of reconnecting to that server.
whyWrong: Round-robin assigns each connection to the next server in the list, so a reconnecting user may reach a different server.
Weighted least connection sends each connection to the server with the fewest weighted connections, not to the user's previous server.
Resource-based balancing sends connections to the least loaded server, not to the user's previous server.
source: CompTIA Security+ Practice Tests: Exam SY0-701 (Seidl) – Chapter 3: Domain 3.0: Security Architecture, Review Questions question 202
note: Load-balancing algorithms are not listed in SY0-801; mapped to load balancing.

stem: Jim wants to design his network for high availability (HA). What first step is commonly taken in HA designs for networks?
explanation: Identifying single points of failure is a common first step in network high-availability designs. It lets designers plan for failures and decide how to avoid them.
whyWrong: Configuring a hot site happens much later, after needs have been identified and prioritized.
Buying redundant hardware comes after the single points of failure that need it have been identified.
Clustering is implemented later in the design, once the needs and failure points are known.
source: CompTIA Security+ Practice Tests: Exam SY0-701 (Seidl) – Chapter 3: Domain 3.0: Security Architecture, Review Questions question 207

stem: Jack is worried about outages that may disrupt service from his IaaS vendor’s cloud environment. Which of the following options provides the greatest likelihood of avoiding service disruptions from an outage from his current IaaS vendor?
explanation: When outages at a single vendor are the main concern, a multi-cloud deployment avoids depending on that vendor. It is costlier and more complex, especially for services customized to one provider, but it is the only option that survives a provider-wide outage.
whyWrong: Multiple availability zones do not avoid an outage when the IaaS vendor has a cloud-wide issue.
Multiple regions within the same vendor do not avoid an outage when the vendor has a cloud-wide issue.
Contractual uptime terms do not stop outages; they usually only give penalties when an outage lasts too long.
source: CompTIA Security+ Practice Tests: Exam SY0-701 (Seidl) – Chapter 3: Domain 3.0: Security Architecture, Review Questions question 211

stem: Chuck is responsible for an on-site datacenter. He wants to ensure that the datacenter has appropriate network connectivity to ensure resilience and performance. Which of the following will have the greatest impact on meeting that requirement?
options: Contract for a higher bandwidth connection from a single vendor.
Contract with two separate network service providers.
explanation: Contracting with two separate network service providers gives resilience, because one connection stays up if the other fails. Traffic can also be sent over both connections for better performance.
whyWrong: A faster connection from one vendor improves performance but leaves a single point of failure for connectivity.
A UPS helps power resilience, but the requirement here is network connectivity.
A generator helps power resilience, but the requirement here is network connectivity.
source: CompTIA Security+ Practice Tests: Exam SY0-701 (Seidl) – Chapter 3: Domain 3.0: Security Architecture, Review Questions question 212

stem: Elaine wants to adopt appropriate response and recovery controls for natural disasters. What type of control should she use to prepare for a multi-hour power outage caused by a tornado?
explanation: A generator is the most appropriate control for a multi-hour power outage. A UPS keeps systems online only long enough for the generator to take over, and a hot site would cost far more than a generator.
whyWrong: A hot site would keep the organization online but costs much more than a generator for a power outage.
A PDU distributes and manages power and does not supply power during an outage.
A UPS is not designed for long outages; it conditions power and bridges the gap until a generator starts.
source: CompTIA Security+ Practice Tests: Exam SY0-701 (Seidl) – Chapter 3: Domain 3.0: Security Architecture, Review Questions question 23

stem: Tim wants to ensure that his web servers can scale horizontally during traffic increases, while also allowing them to be patched or upgraded without causing outages. What type of network device should he deploy?
explanation: A network load balancer distributes traffic among systems and lets systems be added or removed from the pool. Connections can be drained from a server so it can be patched or upgraded without an outage, and new servers can be added as traffic grows.
whyWrong: A firewall is a security device and does not spread traffic across web servers.
A switch forwards traffic to the correct system but does not balance load or let servers be removed without an outage.
A horizontal scaler is not a real type of network device.
source: CompTIA Security+ Practice Tests: Exam SY0-701 (Seidl) – Chapter 3: Domain 3.0: Security Architecture, Review Questions question 24

stem: Olivia is implementing a load-balanced web application cluster. Her organization already has a redundant pair of load balancers, but each unit is not rated to handle the maximum designed throughput of the cluster by itself. Olivia has recommended that the load balancers be implemented in an active/active design. What concern should she raise as part of this recommendation?
options: The load balancer cluster cannot be patched without a service outage.
The load balancer cluster is vulnerable to a denial-of-service attack.
If one of the load balancers fails, it could lead to service degradation.
The load balancer cannot handle the throughput due to having two active nodes.
explanation: In an active/active design, both load balancers carry traffic, and neither can handle the full designed throughput alone. If one fails, the remaining unit cannot carry the whole load, so the service may degrade.
whyWrong: Services rarely run at maximum capacity and maintenance windows can be scheduled, so the pair can still be patched.
An active/active design does not make the load balancers more vulnerable to denial-of-service attacks than other designs.
Two active nodes usually increase throughput compared with a single node.
source: CompTIA Security+ Practice Tests: Exam SY0-701 (Seidl) – Chapter 3: Domain 3.0: Security Architecture, Review Questions question 27

stem: Mark is responsible for managing his company’s load balancer and wants to use a load-balancing scheduling technique that will take into account the current server load and active sessions. Which of the following techniques should he choose?
explanation: Least connection load balancing takes current load into account by sending each new request to the server with the fewest active sessions. It matches the need to consider server load and active sessions.
whyWrong: Round-robin sends requests to each server in turn without considering load or active sessions.
Weighted response time sends traffic to the server that responds fastest in health checks, not by counting active sessions.
Source IP hashing uses a hash of the IP addresses to keep a client on the same server, not to balance by load.
source: CompTIA Security+ Practice Tests: Exam SY0-701 (Seidl) – Chapter 3: Domain 3.0: Security Architecture, Review Questions question 28
note: Load-balancing algorithms are not listed in SY0-801; mapped to load balancing.

stem: What IP address does a load balancer provide for external connections to connect to web servers in a load-balanced group?
options: The IP address for each server, in a prioritized order
The IP address for each server in a round-robin order
explanation: A load balancer provides a virtual IP address (VIP) for external connections. Traffic sent to the VIP is passed to servers in the pool according to the pool's load-balancing method.
whyWrong: Exposing each server's address would let traffic go directly to individual hosts and bypass the load balancer.
The load balancer's own IP address is normally used to administer the device, not for client traffic.
Handing out server addresses in round-robin order is not how a load balancer presents a service; servers stay behind a single virtual address.
source: CompTIA Security+ Practice Tests: Exam SY0-701 (Seidl) – Chapter 3: Domain 3.0: Security Architecture, Review Questions question 35

stem: You are responsible for an e-commerce site. The site is hosted in a cluster. Which of the following techniques would be best in assuring availability?
explanation: Load balancing the cluster keeps any single server from being overloaded. If a server goes offline, the other servers take over its workload, which keeps the site available.
whyWrong: A VPN concentrator creates virtual private network connections and does not keep the cluster available.
Aggregate switching can send more bandwidth to the servers but does not help when servers go offline.
An SSL accelerator offloads TLS encryption work to hardware but does not keep the site available when servers fail.
source: CompTIA Security+ Practice Tests: Exam SY0-701 (Seidl) – Chapter 3: Domain 3.0: Security Architecture, Review Questions question 41

stem: Christina wants to ensure that session persistence is maintained by her load balancer. What is she attempting to do?
options: Ensure that all of a client’s requests go to the same server for the duration of a given session or transaction.
Assign the same internal IP address to clients whenever they connect through the load balancer.
Ensure that all transactions go to the current server in a round-robin during the time it is the primary server.
Assign the same external IP address to all servers whenever they are the primary server assigned by the load balancer.
explanation: Session persistence makes sure that all of a client's traffic for a session or transaction goes to the same server or service. This keeps session data, such as a shopping cart, consistent for the user.
whyWrong: Session persistence is about which server handles a client's requests, not about assigning addresses to clients.
Session persistence keeps a client with one server for the whole session, not with whichever server is current in a round-robin.
Session persistence does not assign the same external address to servers; it keeps a client's requests on one server.
source: CompTIA Security+ Practice Tests: Exam SY0-701 (Seidl) – Chapter 3: Domain 3.0: Security Architecture, Review Questions question 44

stem: Jerome needs to explain the key difference between high availability and fault tolerance to his management. What is the major difference between the two?
options: High availability is designed to avoid service interruptions almost entirely, whereas fault-tolerant environments have minimal service disruptions.
High availability provides services, whereas fault tolerance handles issues.
High availability focuses on data, whereas fault tolerance focuses on infrastructure.
High availability has minimal service interruptions, whereas fault-tolerant environments are designed to avoid service interruptions almost entirely.
explanation: High-availability designs aim to keep service interruptions to a minimum, whereas fault-tolerant designs aim to avoid service interruptions almost entirely. Fault tolerance therefore costs significantly more, and both use hardware and software to keep services available.
whyWrong: This reverses the two: high availability tolerates minimal interruptions, while fault tolerance aims to avoid them almost entirely.
Both high availability and fault tolerance keep services available, so this does not describe a difference.
Both high availability and fault tolerance focus on service availability, not on data versus infrastructure.
source: CompTIA Security+ Practice Tests: Exam SY0-701 (Seidl) – Chapter 3: Domain 3.0: Security Architecture, Review Questions question 54

stem: Marcellus wants to ensure that his organization has sufficient capacity to handle the failure of a web server. What type of technology could he deploy to ensure that individual web server failures are handled gracefully without using an overly complex solution?
explanation: A load balancer handles the failure of an individual web server by moving its load to the functioning servers in the pool. It is a simple solution that matches the size of the problem.
whyWrong: Platform diversity protects against a failure or vulnerability in one vendor or platform, not the failure of a single server.
A multi-cloud system could help but is far more complex than this simple need requires.
A warm site is suited to the failure of a whole datacenter, not one web server.
source: CompTIA Security+ Practice Tests: Exam SY0-701 (Seidl) – Chapter 3: Domain 3.0: Security Architecture, Review Questions question 71

stem: Jill wants to design her organization for high availability. Which of the following design elements best supports power resilience for a high-availability environment for an on-site datacenter?
options: Using UPS systems backed up by generators
Using a warm site on a separate power grid
explanation: UPS systems backed by generators keep systems online during a power outage, even a long one. The UPS covers the outage immediately, and the generator takes over before the batteries run out.
whyWrong: Generators alone do not start fast enough to avoid an outage when power fails.
UPS systems alone run out of battery power during extended outages.
A warm site needs setup time to bring online, so an outage would still occur.
source: CompTIA Security+ Practice Tests: Exam SY0-701 (Seidl) – Chapter 3: Domain 3.0: Security Architecture, Review Questions question 95

stem: All of your organization’s traffic flows through a single connection to the Internet. Which of the following terms best describes this scenario?
explanation: A single point of failure is one weakness that can bring down an entire system and stop it from working. If all traffic flows through one Internet connection, losing that connection cuts off the whole organization.
whyWrong: Cloud computing is the delivery of hosted services over the Internet and does not describe a single connection.
Load balancing spreads traffic across multiple systems, the opposite of everything depending on one connection.
Virtualization runs virtual machines that share a host's resources and does not describe network connectivity.
source: CompTIA Security+ Practice Tests: Exam SY0-701 (Seidl) – Chapter 4: Domain 4.0: Security Operations, Review Questions question 107
note: Single point of failure is not named in SY0-801; mapped to redundancy strategies.

stem: GlobalTech is implementing a disaster recovery plan and wants to ensure continuous availability with no data loss. They have decided to use replication as a backup strategy. Which of the following replication techniques should GlobalTech implement to achieve their objective?
explanation: Synchronous replication writes data to the primary and secondary locations at the same time. Because every write reaches both sites before it completes, no data is lost if the primary site fails.
whyWrong: Daily periodic replication could lose up to a day of data in a disaster.
Asynchronous replication with hourly synchronization could lose up to an hour of data.
Snapshots every 30 minutes could lose up to 30 minutes of data.
source: CompTIA Security+ SY0-701 Practice Tests & PBQs (Gorgotsias) – Chapter 3: Implementation, Practice Questions question 68
note: SY0-701 replication; SY0-801 lists storage without naming replication.

stem: A company stores its customer records in cloud object storage. Its risk assessment says the data must stay available even if a natural disaster takes the provider's entire primary region offline. Which storage replication option BEST meets this need?
options: RAID 1 mirroring on the database server
explanation: Geo-redundant storage keeps copies in the primary region and also copies the data to a secondary region far away. If the whole primary region fails, the copy in the secondary region is still available. Locally and zone-redundant options keep all copies inside one region.
whyWrong: Locally redundant storage keeps all copies in one data center, so a regional disaster would affect every copy.
Zone-redundant storage spreads copies across availability zones in one region but does not protect against the loss of the whole region.
RAID 1 mirrors disks inside one server, which protects against a single disk failure, not a regional disaster.
source: CompTIA Security+ SY0-701 Certification Guide, 3rd edition (Neil) – Chapter 13: Explain the importance of resilience and recovery in security architecture

stem: Cybertech Corp. is reviewing its backup protocols to enhance security. They decided that before transferring backups to an offsite location, the data should be rendered unreadable to unauthorized individuals. Which backup strategy will ensure this requirement is met?
explanation: Encryption turns data into a form that only someone with the decryption key can read. Encrypting backups before they are transferred offsite keeps them unreadable even if unauthorized people get access to them.
whyWrong: Deduplication removes redundant data to save storage space but does not make the data unreadable.
Proprietary formats may hide data from some people but do not give the strong protection that encryption does.
Compression with standard tools saves space but does not keep the data confidential.
source: CompTIA Security+ SY0-701 Practice Tests & PBQs (Gorgotsias) – Chapter 3: Implementation, Practice Questions question 54
note: Encrypting backups is mapped to the SY0-801 backups topic.

stem: DataFin, a financial analytics firm, experienced a minor fire incident in one of its server rooms. Fortunately, they had backups stored in another wing of the building, allowing for quick data recovery. However, management realizes that in a major disaster, both primary and backup data might be destroyed. To address this, which backup strategy should DataFin consider?
explanation: Offsite backups are stored in a different geographic location from the primary data. If a major disaster affects the primary site, the backups remain safe and can be used for recovery.
whyWrong: A mirror backup is an exact copy of the source data and says nothing about where the copy is stored.
Local storage keeps backups in the same building or nearby, so a major disaster could destroy them with the primary data.
An incremental backup copies only the data changed since the last backup and does not address where backups are stored.
source: CompTIA Security+ SY0-701 Practice Tests & PBQs (Gorgotsias) – Chapter 3: Implementation, Practice Questions question 60

stem: XYZ Corp recently faced a ransomware attack that encrypted critical data files. The company’s IT team was unable to decrypt the files but had a recent backup available. However, when they tried to restore the data, they found out the backup was corrupted. Which of the following best practices would have helped XYZ Corp in ensuring the integrity of their backups?
options: Storing backups in the same directory as original files
Increasing the frequency of backups to every hour
Encrypting backups with a strong encryption algorithm
explanation: Regularly testing the backup restoration process shows whether backups can actually be restored. Problems with the backup files or the process are found and fixed before a real recovery depends on them.
whyWrong: Storing backups beside the original files makes it more likely that both are corrupted or encrypted at the same time.
More frequent backups reduce data loss but do not show whether the backups are valid and usable.
Encrypting backups protects them from unauthorized access but does not ensure that they are intact or usable.
source: CompTIA Security+ SY0-701 Practice Tests & PBQs (Gorgotsias) – Chapter 3: Implementation, Practice Questions question 73

stem: After a major outage, CloudTech Services is reviewing their disaster recovery strategy. The company found out that after restoring from backup, several applications did not function properly due to configuration discrepancies. What would be the best approach to ensure a successful recovery in the future?
options: Prioritize applications for backup based on their importance
Implement differential backups in addition to full backups
Regularly conduct a full system recovery in a test environment
Use a third-party backup solution instead of an in-house solution
explanation: A full system recovery in a test environment simulates a real recovery. It reveals configuration discrepancies and application dependencies that regular backups miss, so they can be fixed before a real recovery is needed.
whyWrong: Prioritizing applications by importance does not find configuration discrepancies or dependencies between applications.
Differential backups capture changes but do not reveal the configuration discrepancies found during recovery.
A third-party backup product does not by itself guarantee a successful recovery or fix configuration discrepancies.
source: CompTIA Security+ SY0-701 Practice Tests & PBQs (Gorgotsias) – Chapter 3: Implementation, Practice Questions question 79

stem: SecureData Inc., a financial firm, recently experienced a system crash and needed to restore their database. While they had a full backup from the previous week, they realized that several days of transactions were missing. To prevent such data loss in the future, which backup strategy involving recording transactions can SecureData implement?
explanation: Journaling keeps a log, or journal, of every transaction or change as it happens. After a crash, the database is restored from the last backup and the journal is replayed to reapply each transaction, which prevents the loss of the days between backups.
whyWrong: Differential backups capture changes since the last full backup at set times but do not record every transaction as it happens.
Hourly snapshots shrink the data loss window but still do not capture every transaction as it occurs.
RAID 5 protects against a disk failure but does not record database transactions for replay.
source: CompTIA Security+ SY0-701 Practice Tests & PBQs (Gorgotsias) – Chapter 3: Implementation, Practice Questions question 84
note: SY0-701 term: journaling (3.4 backups); SY0-801 3.4 lists backups without naming journaling.

stem: MetroTech recently experienced an incident where an employee mistakenly deleted a portion of their database. The IT team was able to restore the data using a backup snapshot taken 24 hours prior. However, some data loss still occurred. Which of the following recommendations would minimize data loss in a similar situation in the future?
options: Configure backup snapshots to be taken on a weekly basis
Employ a differential backup solution in addition to snapshots
Increase the storage capacity for backups
Use an hourly snapshot backup schedule
explanation: Taking snapshots more often, for example every hour, limits the data that can be lost to the changes made since the last snapshot. An hourly schedule shrinks the loss window from 24 hours to at most one hour.
whyWrong: Weekly snapshots would make the potential data loss window larger, not smaller.
Adding differential backups does not by itself shorten the time between recovery points the way more frequent snapshots do.
More backup storage allows more or longer-kept backups but does not shorten the data loss window.
source: CompTIA Security+ SY0-701 Practice Tests & PBQs (Gorgotsias) – Chapter 3: Implementation, Practice Questions question 90

stem: What does an onsite backup strategy offer as a benefit?
options: Fast access to backups for quick recovery
explanation: Onsite backups are kept at the same location as the systems they protect, so they can be reached and restored quickly. This fast access shortens recovery from common failures such as a deleted file or a failed server.
whyWrong: Onsite backups are exposed to the same local disaster as the systems, so protection against local disasters is the benefit of offsite backups.
Encryption is a separate control that can be applied to any backup, wherever it is stored.
Backups hold copies from a point in time, so storing them onsite does not give real-time data availability.
source: CompTIA Security+ SY0-701 Cert Guide (Heuermann) – Chapter 13: Understanding the Importance of Resilience and Recovery in Security Architecture, Do I Know This Already? Quiz question 7
note: SY0-701 term: onsite/offsite backups; SY0-801 3.4 backups do not name onsite/offsite. The book quiz has no key; answer written from the chapter.

stem: A legal department has been advised by a third-party auditor that it needs to maintain a log of all incoming and outgoing emails, due to data compliance. This data must be retained for a period of three years. Which of the following is the BEST solution?
explanation: Email journaling captures and records a copy of every incoming and outgoing email as it is sent or received. It is the usual method for compliance, because every message is logged and can be retained for the required three years.
whyWrong: Weekly backups capture only the mailbox state at backup time, so emails sent and deleted between backups would be missed.
Daily backups are better than weekly ones but still miss emails that are sent and deleted between backups.
Clustering provides high availability and load balancing for servers and is not a method for compliance logging or retention.
source: CompTIA Security+ SY0-701 Certification Guide, 3rd edition (Neil) – Chapter 13: Explain the importance of resilience and recovery in security architecture, Chapter Review Questions question 6
note: SY0-701 term: journaling; SY0-801 3.4 backups list retention but do not name journaling.

stem: Which of the following is the BEST backup and restore solution to utilize in a Virtual Desktop Infrastructure (VDI) environment?
explanation: A snapshot captures a point-in-time image of a virtual desktop, so it is a quick and efficient way to back up and restore in a VDI environment. It lets the administrator return a desktop to a known state if there is a problem or data loss.
whyWrong: A full daily backup of every virtual desktop uses a lot of resources and time and restores more slowly than a snapshot.
A failover cluster provides high availability but does not restore a desktop to an earlier state.
A differential backup is a traditional file backup method and is slower to restore a whole virtual desktop than a snapshot.
source: CompTIA Security+ SY0-701 Certification Guide, 3rd edition (Neil) – Chapter 13: Explain the importance of resilience and recovery in security architecture, Chapter Review Questions question 9
note: Snapshots are not named in SY0-801 3.4 backups.

stem: What type of backup is done to update a full backup with changes made after the full backup occurred?
explanation: An incremental backup copies only the data that has changed since the previous backup, and the chain of incremental backups brings the last full backup up to date. To restore, the full backup is restored first and then each incremental backup is applied in order from oldest to newest.
whyWrong: A partial backup copies only certain data or parts of a system and is not defined by changes made after a full backup.
A daily backup describes how often a backup runs, and it may be full, incremental, or differential.
Snapshots are point-in-time images of a system's data and state, not updates applied to a full backup.
source: CompTIA Security+ Practice Tests: Exam SY0-701 (Seidl) – Chapter 3: Domain 3.0: Security Architecture, Review Questions question 102
note: Book key kept, but the book explanation defined incremental backups as changes since the last full backup (the differential definition); the explanation was rewritten.

stem: Madhuri has configured a backup that will back up all of the changes to a system since the last time that a full backup occurred. What type of backup has she set up?
explanation: A differential backup copies all of the changes made since the last full backup. Each differential grows until the next full backup, and a restore needs only the full backup plus the latest differential.
whyWrong: A snapshot captures a machine's state and full drive at a point in time rather than only the changes since a full backup.
A full backup is a complete copy of the system, not just the changes since the last full backup.
An incremental backup copies only the changes since the last backup of any type, not all changes since the last full backup.
source: CompTIA Security+ Practice Tests: Exam SY0-701 (Seidl) – Chapter 3: Domain 3.0: Security Architecture, Review Questions question 15

stem: Theresa wants to back up her virtualization environment. What backup scheme is most frequently used for virtual machines?
explanation: Snapshots are the backup scheme most often used for virtual machines, because they copy both the VM's data and its machine state at a point in time. A VM can be rolled back to a snapshot quickly.
whyWrong: Journaling records transactions for replay and is used mainly with databases, not as the main backup scheme for VMs.
Replication keeps a synchronous or asynchronous copy of data available but is not the usual VM backup scheme.
Grandfather/Father/Son is a backup rotation cycle commonly used for tape backups.
source: CompTIA Security+ Practice Tests: Exam SY0-701 (Seidl) – Chapter 3: Domain 3.0: Security Architecture, Review Questions question 153
note: Snapshots are not named in SY0-801 3.4 backups.

stem: Erin uses a journaling backup scheme for her database. After a system outage she needs to restore from her backups. If her organization uses a daily backup scheme that runs at midnight, and the issue occurred at 2 a.m., how much data is Erin likely to lose?
options: One day and two hours of data
explanation: Journaling records transactions as they occur. Unless the journal itself is lost, Erin can restore the midnight backup and then replay the journal, so the organization loses little or no data.
whyWrong: Two hours of data would be lost only without the journal, which replays the transactions made after midnight.
The daily backup ran at midnight, and the journal covers the time after it, so far less than a day is lost.
A week of data would be lost only if no daily backup or journal existed.
source: CompTIA Security+ Practice Tests: Exam SY0-701 (Seidl) – Chapter 3: Domain 3.0: Security Architecture, Review Questions question 175
note: SY0-701 term: journaling; not named in SY0-801 3.4 backups. The book explanation named the wrong person (Melissa); corrected to Erin.

stem: Maria’s organization uses a cloud backup provider and performs encrypted backups for their IaaS infrastructure and data. If the data needs to be restored, what will Maria need to do?
options: Ask the vendor for the recovery key.
Restore the recovery key from backup and use it.
Generate a new recovery key and restore from backup.
explanation: Encrypted backups can be restored only with the encryption key, so Maria's organization must provide the recovery key that it keeps. The key must be stored securely and separately from the backups, for example as physical copies in secured, geographically diverse places or in a key management system.
whyWrong: The organization encrypts the backups itself, so the vendor does not hold the recovery key.
A recovery key stored only inside the encrypted backups could not be reached when the backups need it.
A new key cannot decrypt backups that were encrypted with the original key.
source: CompTIA Security+ Practice Tests: Exam SY0-701 (Seidl) – Chapter 3: Domain 3.0: Security Architecture, Review Questions question 177

stem: What two major differences separate backups and replication?
options: Replication is periodic, but does not require restoration processes before data is able to be used.
Backups are continuous but require restoration processes before data is able to be used.
Backups are periodic and do not require restoration before data is able to be used
Replication is continuous and does not require restoration processes before data is able to be used.
explanation: Replication is a continuous process, so the replica can be used without restoration work. Backups are periodic and usually need restoration, such as restoring a full backup and then applying differentials or journals, before the data can be used.
whyWrong: Replication is continuous, not periodic.
Backups are periodic, not continuous.
Backups usually need restoration processes before the data can be used.
source: CompTIA Security+ Practice Tests: Exam SY0-701 (Seidl) – Chapter 3: Domain 3.0: Security Architecture, Review Questions question 178
note: Replication is not named in SY0-801 3.4 backups.

stem: Erin’s organization uses a backup schedule that creates a full backup once a week, then creates differential backups once a day on all other days. If the full backup was done four days ago, and Erin needs to restore from it, how many backups will she have to restore in total?
explanation: Each differential backup holds all of the changes made since the last full backup. To restore, Erin needs the full backup plus only the most recent differential, for a total of two backups.
whyWrong: The full backup alone would miss the changes made in the days after it.
The earlier differentials are not needed, because the latest differential already contains all of their changes.
Restoring every daily differential is what an incremental schedule requires, not a differential one.
source: CompTIA Security+ Practice Tests: Exam SY0-701 (Seidl) – Chapter 3: Domain 3.0: Security Architecture, Review Questions question 179
note: Book key: D (four); corrected to B (two) because each differential contains all changes since the full backup, so only the full and the latest differential are restored. Explanation rewritten.

stem: Which of the following is not available as part of a snapshot?
explanation: A virtual machine snapshot captures the VM's power state, memory state, and disks. The configuration of the underlying hypervisor is not part of the VM, so a snapshot does not capture it.
whyWrong: The VM's power state is captured as part of a snapshot.
The VM's memory state is captured as part of a snapshot.
The VM's disks are captured as part of a snapshot.
source: CompTIA Security+ Practice Tests: Exam SY0-701 (Seidl) – Chapter 3: Domain 3.0: Security Architecture, Review Questions question 194
note: Snapshots are not named in SY0-801 3.4 backups.

stem: Angela is considering using encryption as part of the security controls applied to her backups. In the event of a major disaster, what concern should she address about having encrypted backups?
options: Ensuring the key is recoverable in a disaster
The amount of space that the encryption adds to the backups
explanation: The main concern with encrypted backups is whether the keys will be available in a disaster. The keys must be stored so that they can be recovered whenever the backups are recovered, or the backups cannot be used.
whyWrong: Modern backup encryption does not add a meaningful amount of time to decryption.
The cost of encrypting backups is low and is not the main disaster concern.
Encryption does not add enough space to backups to be a primary concern.
source: CompTIA Security+ Practice Tests: Exam SY0-701 (Seidl) – Chapter 3: Domain 3.0: Security Architecture, Review Questions question 209

stem: Nick’s organization houses tape-based backups for their critical data in their primary datacenter. What resilience issue could result in the event of a major disaster?
options: The tapes may not have been validated and might not be able to be restored.
A single disaster could destroy both the facility and the tapes.
The tapes may not last for the expected lifetime of the backups.
Tapes are relatively slow and may not allow for timely restoration.
explanation: Keeping backups in the same facility as the systems they protect means that a single disaster could destroy both. Nick should consider storing the backups off-site.
whyWrong: Backup validation can be a concern, but nothing in the question suggests the tapes were not tested.
Tapes typically last longer than the period for which most organizations keep backups.
Slow tape restoration affects the restoration timeframe, not the resilience of the backups.
source: CompTIA Security+ Practice Tests: Exam SY0-701 (Seidl) – Chapter 3: Domain 3.0: Security Architecture, Review Questions question 77

stem: Mike is a security analyst and has just removed malware from a virtual server. What feature of virtualization would he use to return the virtual server to a last known good state?
explanation: A snapshot is an image of a virtual machine at a point in time. Administrators take snapshots periodically so they can return a VM to a last known good state, for example after removing malware.
whyWrong: Sandboxing isolates a system or software and does not return a server to an earlier state.
The hypervisor is the layer through which virtual machines use the hardware, not a way to restore a VM's state.
Elasticity is the ability of a system to scale resources up and down.
source: CompTIA Security+ Practice Tests: Exam SY0-701 (Seidl) – Chapter 3: Domain 3.0: Security Architecture, Review Questions question 8
note: Snapshots are not named in SY0-801 3.4 backups.

stem: Pete’s organization has had a system fail and Pete wants to recover from backup. Which of the following backup methods will typically result in the fastest restoration timeframe?
explanation: Replication is typically the fastest way to recover, because the replica system is already running and ready to take over. Snapshot recovery is usually next, followed by restoring from other storage.
whyWrong: Snapshot recovery is fast but usually slower than switching to a running replica.
Journaling can slow restoration because the journal must be replayed from the last backup to the time of failure.
Tape backup is one of the slowest restoration methods.
source: CompTIA Security+ Practice Tests: Exam SY0-701 (Seidl) – Chapter 3: Domain 3.0: Security Architecture, Review Questions question 81
note: Replication is not named in SY0-801 3.4 backups.

stem: Yuri wants to use an off-site backup location. What challenge can off-site backup locations create for organizations?
options: It is difficult to validate the integrity of the backups.
Retrieving the backups may slow down recovery.
The backups cannot be easily updated.
Off-site backups may be impacted by the same disaster.
explanation: Off-site backup locations are chosen so that the same disaster will not affect them. The trade-off is that recovery may be slow, because the backups must be physically retrieved or downloaded over an Internet connection.
whyWrong: Backup integrity is usually verified as part of the backup process and can be checked easily.
Off-site backups are updated as part of the normal backup process.
Off-site locations are chosen specifically so that the same disaster does not affect them.
source: CompTIA Security+ Practice Tests: Exam SY0-701 (Seidl) – Chapter 3: Domain 3.0: Security Architecture, Review Questions question 91

stem: What is the biggest downside of using journaling as part of a backup restoration process?
options: Larger volumes of data may be lost.
The time it takes to restore from a journal.
Journals cannot be encrypted for security.
Journaling does not support live databases.
explanation: Restoring with a journal means replaying the recorded transactions, which can take a long time when much time has passed since the last backup and there were many transactions. Journaling therefore trades a longer restoration for very little data loss.
whyWrong: Journaling minimizes the amount of transaction data that is lost rather than increasing it.
Journals can be encrypted, although the keys must stay recoverable.
Journaling is used with live databases to recover transactions up to the point of failure.
source: CompTIA Security+ Practice Tests: Exam SY0-701 (Seidl) – Chapter 3: Domain 3.0: Security Architecture, Review Questions question 94
note: SY0-701 term: journaling; not named in SY0-801 3.4 backups.

stem: After a major power outage, TechWave Corp. wants to ensure their primary data center’s operations can be swiftly and seamlessly shifted to another facility. The company wants this process to be automated and immediate to prevent any service interruption. What type of test should TechWave Corp. conduct to validate this functionality?
options: Conduct a vulnerability assessment on both data centers
explanation: A failover test simulates a failure of the primary system to confirm that the backup site or system takes over automatically without a service interruption. It verifies the resilience and recovery capabilities of the infrastructure.
whyWrong: A vulnerability assessment finds weaknesses in systems but does not test the switch from the primary to the backup facility.
A tabletop exercise is a discussion-based session and does not test live systems.
A routine backup test confirms that backups can be restored but not that operations switch over immediately.
source: CompTIA Security+ SY0-701 Practice Tests & PBQs (Gorgotsias) – Chapter 3: Implementation, Practice Questions question 55

stem: After a recent system upgrade, CloudTech Corp. decided to validate the efficiency and reliability of its new data processing system. To do this, they run the new system alongside the old one and compare the outcomes. This way, they aim to ensure that the new system is both robust and capable of handling the current workload. What kind of testing is CloudTech Corp. utilizing?
explanation: Parallel processing testing runs the new system alongside the old one and compares their outcomes. It confirms that the new system is as reliable and effective as the old one before the old one is retired.
whyWrong: Load testing checks whether a system can handle the expected volume of transactions with acceptable response times, not whether two systems give the same results.
Failover testing checks that a system can switch to a backup system after a failure rather than comparing two systems.
Simulation testing models a scenario to see how a system or team behaves under certain conditions rather than running two systems side by side.
source: CompTIA Security+ SY0-701 Practice Tests & PBQs (Gorgotsias) – Chapter 3: Implementation, Practice Questions question 65

stem: SecureNet Inc. recently upgraded their security infrastructure. To validate how the new system would respond in real-world scenarios without exposing it to actual risks, they decide to imitate certain cyber threats in a controlled environment. Which type of test is SecureNet Inc. planning to conduct?
explanation: Simulation testing imitates conditions, such as cyber threats, in a controlled environment to see how a system responds. It lets SecureNet assess its new security infrastructure without exposing it to actual risks.
whyWrong: Penetration testing involves ethical hackers actually trying to breach defenses, which carries real risk.
A vulnerability assessment identifies and prioritizes weaknesses but does not imitate threats.
Failover testing confirms that a system can switch to a backup after a failure and does not imitate threats.
source: CompTIA Security+ SY0-701 Practice Tests & PBQs (Gorgotsias) – Chapter 3: Implementation, Practice Questions question 85

stem: You are managing a large-scale scientific simulation project that requires you to perform complex calculations on massive datasets. To optimize the project’s performance, you need to choose the right processing technique. Which technique would be most effective to accelerate your simulation’s calculations and manage the massive datasets efficiently?
explanation: Parallel processing breaks large calculations into smaller tasks and runs them at the same time on multiple processors. This greatly speeds up the simulation and handles massive datasets efficiently.
whyWrong: Sequential processing runs tasks one after another, which slows down the simulation.
Multithreading allows concurrent execution but may not fully use multiple processors.
Batch processing handles large volumes of data in groups but does not run the calculations in parallel.
source: CompTIA Security+ SY0-701 Certification Guide, 3rd edition (Neil) – Chapter 13: Explain the importance of resilience and recovery in security architecture, Chapter Review Questions question 7
note: The book question uses parallel processing as a computing technique; SY0-801 3.4 lists parallel processing under testing.

stem: As part of an exercise for her organization, Sharon calls a team member and asks them to check the status of critical systems. The team member, who is aware of the exercise, does not actually validate the systems but responds that specific systems are down based on the scenario. What type of exercise is Sharon most likely part of?
explanation: In a simulation exercise, participants act out how they would respond to a scenario without taking real actions, such as reporting systems as down instead of checking them. It is safer than a failover or parallel processing test but closer to a real event than a tabletop exercise.
whyWrong: A tabletop exercise is a discussion around a table, without participants being called to act out their responses.
A failover exercise actually moves operations to backup systems rather than pretending systems are down.
A parallel processing test runs live systems side by side and does not involve role-played responses.
source: CompTIA Security+ Practice Tests: Exam SY0-701 (Seidl) – Chapter 3: Domain 3.0: Security Architecture, Review Questions question 103

stem: Lucca wants to fully validate his organization’s hot site’s ability to perform as needed in the event of an outage. What type of testing should he run to ensure that the hot site is completely tested as though an actual disaster has occurred?
explanation: Failover testing completely moves running services to the hot site, as would happen in an actual disaster. It is the most complex and risky testing mode, but it is the only one that fully tests the site in a real-world exercise.
whyWrong: A simulation acts out the response to a scenario without actually moving services to the hot site.
A tabletop exercise discusses the response and does not test the site itself.
Parallel processing runs systems side by side without the hot site fully taking over operations.
source: CompTIA Security+ Practice Tests: Exam SY0-701 (Seidl) – Chapter 3: Domain 3.0: Security Architecture, Review Questions question 143

stem: What is the primary reason an organization might choose a parallel processing testing scenario over a fail over testing scenario?
options: Parallel processing allows for more throughput.
Fail over does not fully test redundant systems.
Fail over requires organizations to create a significant issue to allow for the fail over to occur.
Parallel processing typically handles issues without outages.
explanation: Parallel processing tests systems without taking them offline. If the backup systems or facility have a problem during the test, the primary facility keeps operating, so issues are handled without an outage.
whyWrong: Parallel processing does add throughput, but the environment must be able to carry the full load alone, so this is not the reason to choose it for testing.
Failover testing does fully test redundant systems.
Failover tests use a manual failover process rather than requiring a significant issue to be created.
source: CompTIA Security+ Practice Tests: Exam SY0-701 (Seidl) – Chapter 3: Domain 3.0: Security Architecture, Review Questions question 154

stem: Elle is conducting an exercise for her organization and wants to run an exercise that is as close to an actual event as possible. What type of event should she run to help her organization get this type of real-world practice?
explanation: A simulation is the closest an organization can get to a real-world event without having one. Participants act out the response to the scenario.
whyWrong: A tabletop exercise has personnel discussing a scenario rather than acting it out.
A walk-through goes through checklists and procedures and is further from a real event.
A wargame is not a common exercise type for continuity testing.
source: CompTIA Security+ Practice Tests: Exam SY0-701 (Seidl) – Chapter 3: Domain 3.0: Security Architecture, Review Questions question 170

stem: Mateo wants to conduct a fail over test for his datacenter. What will he need to do to accomplish this?
options: Turn off all systems in his datacenter.
Simulate what would occur during a datacenter outage.
Force a fail over using his network or other systems.
Cause an outage of a critical system.
explanation: Datacenters should have a failover process that can be run manually in an emergency. Mateo should use that process to force a failover to his organization's failover site.
whyWrong: Turning off every system in a datacenter is not recommended because it may cause other unexpected failures.
A simulation acts out an outage but does not actually fail over.
An outage of one critical system typically does not cause an entire datacenter to fail over.
source: CompTIA Security+ Practice Tests: Exam SY0-701 (Seidl) – Chapter 3: Domain 3.0: Security Architecture, Review Questions question 57

stem: Ramon wants to conduct an exercise for his organization with the least potential to cause disruption. Which of the following testing methodologies is least likely to cause potential issues with service delivery?
explanation: Tabletop exercises are talked through in a room and do not involve real technical systems. This makes them the least likely exercise type to disrupt service delivery.
whyWrong: Failover exercises move live services to other systems and can affect service delivery.
Simulation exercises need care because simulated calls or commands can accidentally become real actions.
Parallel processing exercises run on live systems and can affect service delivery.
source: CompTIA Security+ Practice Tests: Exam SY0-701 (Seidl) – Chapter 3: Domain 3.0: Security Architecture, Review Questions question 64

stem: Selah’s organization is conducting a simulation exercise. Which of the following is not a common element of a simulation?
explanation: Simulations act out a scenario while trying to avoid causing real outages. They may check that notification processes, communication systems, and procedures work, but they do not test failover capabilities.
whyWrong: Testing notification processes is a common element of a simulation.
Testing procedures is a common element of a simulation.
Testing communication systems is a common element of a simulation.
source: CompTIA Security+ Practice Tests: Exam SY0-701 (Seidl) – Chapter 3: Domain 3.0: Security Architecture, Review Questions question 68

stem: How does a disaster recovery plan relate to a business continuity plan?
options: It is a subset of business continuity that focuses on restoring IT systems and data after a disaster
It replaces the business continuity plan for events that affect only one department
It covers only how employees and the media are told about the disaster
It is the same document under a different name used by IT teams
explanation: Business continuity covers how the whole organization keeps its essential functions running during a disruption. Disaster recovery is a subset of it that focuses on the technical work of restoring IT infrastructure, systems, and data so normal operations can resume. A disaster recovery plan or policy also defines items such as off-site data storage and the roles of the disaster recovery team.
whyWrong: Disaster recovery does not replace business continuity; it supports it for IT systems.
Notifying employees and the media belongs to a communication plan, not the technical recovery of systems.
The two plans differ in scope: continuity covers business functions, recovery covers IT restoration.
source: CompTIA Security+ SY0-701 Cert Guide (Heuermann) – Chapter 23: Summarizing Elements of Effective Security Governance; CompTIA Security+ SY0-701 Certification Guide, 3rd edition (Neil) – Chapter 13: Explain the importance of resilience and recovery in security architecture

stem: A flood destroyed a company's server room. Management has already moved staff to temporary offices, and the IT team now needs documented steps to restore servers and data from off-site backups at the recovery site. Which document BEST guides the IT team?
explanation: A disaster recovery plan holds the technical procedures to restore IT infrastructure, systems, and data after a disaster, such as recovering from off-site backups at a recovery site. It also names the members and roles of the disaster recovery team. It works as part of the wider business continuity effort that keeps the business running.
whyWrong: An incident response plan guides the handling of security incidents such as malware or breaches, not rebuilding after a natural disaster.
An acceptable use policy tells users how they may use company systems and has no recovery steps.
Change management controls planned changes to systems and does not describe recovery after a disaster.
source: CompTIA Security+ SY0-701 Cert Guide (Heuermann) – Chapter 23: Summarizing Elements of Effective Security Governance; CompTIA Security+ SY0-701 Certification Guide, 3rd edition (Neil) – Chapter 13: Explain the importance of resilience and recovery in security architecture

stem: A global corporation has undergone several IT incidents in the past year, including outages due to natural disasters and cyber attacks. The CEO wants to ensure the organization’s IT infrastructure can withstand or rapidly recover from disruptive events. Which of the following best encapsulates this requirement?
options: Establishing a Business Continuity Plan (BCP) with emphasis on resilience
explanation: Resilience is the ability of the IT infrastructure to withstand disruptive events or recover quickly and keep functioning. A business continuity plan that emphasizes resilience prepares the organization to respond to and recover from both natural and human-made incidents.
whyWrong: Zero Trust architecture removes implicit trust for users and systems but does not directly address recovery from disruptive events.
A strict password policy improves account security but does not help the infrastructure withstand outages or disasters.
Updating firewall rules blocks unwanted traffic but does not make the infrastructure resilient to major disruptions.
source: CompTIA Security+ SY0-701 Practice Tests & PBQs (Gorgotsias) – Chapter 3: Implementation, Practice Questions question 45

stem: What does COOP address?
explanation: A continuity of operations plan (COOP) addresses emergencies from an all-hazards approach. It sets policy and guidance so that critical functions continue and personnel and resources can be moved to an alternate facility whatever the cause of the emergency.
whyWrong: COOP covers all hazards, not only natural disasters.
COOP covers all hazards, not only cybersecurity attacks.
Relocating to an alternate facility is one part of COOP, not its whole scope.
source: CompTIA Security+ SY0-701 Cert Guide (Heuermann) – Chapter 13: Understanding the Importance of Resilience and Recovery in Security Architecture, Do I Know This Already? Quiz question 2
note: SY0-701 term: continuity of operations planning (COOP); SY0-801 3.4 lists business continuity. The book quiz has no key; answer written from the chapter.

stem: Ed is building a continuity of operations plan (COOP) for his organization. What three scenarios does a COOP address?
options: Loss of personnel, loss of systems, loss of availability
Natural disasters, human-made disasters, mistakes or errors
Loss of access to a facility, damage to a facility, natural disasters
Loss of access to a facility, loss of personnel, and loss of services
explanation: A COOP plan addresses the loss of access to some or all of a facility, the loss of personnel, and the loss of services. Many events can cause these losses, but the plan focuses on keeping the key parts of the organization (facilities, staff, and services) operating.
whyWrong: Loss of systems and loss of availability are outcomes of the losses COOP plans for, not its three core scenarios.
Natural disasters, human-made disasters, and mistakes are causes of disruption, not the scenarios a COOP is organized around.
Facility damage and natural disasters are causes of losing a facility, and the list leaves out personnel and services.
source: CompTIA Security+ Practice Tests: Exam SY0-701 (Seidl) – Chapter 3: Domain 3.0: Security Architecture, Review Questions question 126
note: SY0-701 term: continuity of operations planning (COOP); SY0-801 3.4 lists business continuity.

stem: Laura is planning for continuity of operations. What personnel concern should she plan to handle for her hot site in the event of a large-scale natural disaster in the area where her primary facility is?
explanation: In a large-scale disaster, personnel may be unable or unwilling to report to work, because the disaster also affects where they live. Continuity plans for a disaster in the area where staff live and work must include ways to ensure enough staff are available.
whyWrong: Lack of facility power is an infrastructure concern, not a personnel concern.
Authenticating personnel should already be part of the hot site's capabilities.
Insider threats are not a common concern during natural disasters.
source: CompTIA Security+ Practice Tests: Exam SY0-701 (Seidl) – Chapter 3: Domain 3.0: Security Architecture, Review Questions question 172

stem: DigitalFront, an e-commerce company, is expecting a surge in traffic during their upcoming annual sale event. They want to ensure that their website and applications can handle the anticipated increase in user activity without any performance degradation. Which of the following steps is MOST relevant to achieving this goal?
options: Increasing the frequency of security audits
Implementing capacity planning specifically focused on technology
Adopting multi-factor authentication for all users
Investing in advanced threat intelligence solutions
explanation: Technology capacity planning makes sure that servers, bandwidth, storage, and software are ready for the expected increase in load. This keeps the website and applications performing well during the peak of the sale event.
whyWrong: Security audits find vulnerabilities but do not scale resources to handle more traffic.
Multifactor authentication improves account security but does not help handle a surge in traffic.
Threat intelligence gives insight into potential threats but does not add capacity for more users.
source: CompTIA Security+ SY0-701 Practice Tests & PBQs (Gorgotsias) – Chapter 3: Implementation, Practice Questions question 63

stem: TechSolutions Inc., a rapidly growing startup, is expanding its workforce to meet its customer demands. As part of this expansion, they need to ensure their IT infrastructure can accommodate the influx of new employees without compromising performance or security. Which of the following should be TechSolutions’ primary focus during this expansion phase?
options: Adopting a Zero Trust Network Architecture
Increasing the frequency of vulnerability assessments
Deploying additional firewalls and intrusion detection systems
explanation: Capacity planning makes sure that an organization's infrastructure, technology, and people scale to meet growth and performance needs. With an influx of new employees, TechSolutions must make sure its IT infrastructure can handle the extra demand.
whyWrong: Zero Trust architecture may improve security but does not scale resources for new employees.
Vulnerability assessments are important for security but do not address the infrastructure's ability to handle growth.
More firewalls and intrusion detection systems improve security but do not add capacity for more employees.
source: CompTIA Security+ SY0-701 Practice Tests & PBQs (Gorgotsias) – Chapter 3: Implementation, Practice Questions question 66

stem: StreamNet, a popular online streaming service, is planning to launch in three new countries. They anticipate a substantial increase in users and concurrent streams. To ensure that the service remains uninterrupted and provides a seamless experience to new users, which action related to capacity planning should StreamNet prioritize?
options: Investing in content encryption and DRM
Increasing marketing and promotional activities in the new countries
Expanding and optimizing their infrastructure to handle the projected growth
explanation: Infrastructure capacity planning predicts the resources needed for the expected growth and guides upgrades to servers, networks, storage, and other components. Expanding and optimizing the infrastructure keeps the service smooth as new users join.
