whyWrong: Content encryption and DRM protect the content but do not add the capacity needed for more users.
Marketing attracts users but does not affect the infrastructure's capacity to serve them.
Stronger authentication improves security but does not address capacity or scalability.
source: CompTIA Security+ SY0-701 Practice Tests & PBQs (Gorgotsias) – Chapter 3: Implementation, Practice Questions question 67

stem: What is the focus of technology in capacity planning?
explanation: Technology capacity planning evaluates the computational power, software, and hardware an organization needs to meet future demands. It analyzes usage patterns and forecasts needs so the organization is neither overprovisioned nor underprovisioned.
whyWrong: Staffing needs are the focus of people capacity planning, not technology capacity planning.
Infrastructure planning is a separate area of capacity planning, alongside people and technology.
Future cloud storage is only one small part of technology capacity planning.
source: CompTIA Security+ SY0-701 Cert Guide (Heuermann) – Chapter 13: Understanding the Importance of Resilience and Recovery in Security Architecture, Do I Know This Already? Quiz question 3
note: The book quiz has no key; answer written from the chapter.

stem: During a meeting of all department heads, the CEO of a company requests information regarding staffing needs to relocate the entire company to an alternative hot site following a disaster. Which of the following BEST describes the CEO’s primary objective in seeking this information?
explanation: The CEO wants to know how many staff are needed to run the company from the hot site, which is people capacity planning. Capacity planning makes sure that enough resources, including staff, are available for a smooth transition and continued operation after a disaster.
whyWrong: Business continuity is closely related but is the broader goal, not the specific question of how many staff are needed.
Labor costing calculates labor expenses, which is not what the CEO asked about.
Operational load distribution spreads computing workloads across resources and does not concern staffing.
source: CompTIA Security+ SY0-701 Certification Guide, 3rd edition (Neil) – Chapter 13: Explain the importance of resilience and recovery in security architecture, Chapter Review Questions question 3

stem: Julia is designing her organization’s external connectivity as part of infrastructure capacity planning. She knows that the organization typically uses approximately 7 gigabits per second of connectivity from their primary site. Julia has the following connectivity options, what should she select?
options: A 10 Gbps primary and a 5 Gbps secondary connection
A 5 Gbps primary and a 5 Gbps secondary connection
A 100 Gbps primary and a 10 Gbps secondary connection
A 10 Gbps primary and a 10 Gbps secondary connection
explanation: Failover connections should be able to carry the organization's full throughput, so both links must handle about 7 Gbps. Two 10 Gbps connections do this without the large extra cost of 100 Gbps links and the network devices they need.
whyWrong: A 5 Gbps secondary connection could not carry the full 7 Gbps load after a failover.
Two 5 Gbps connections are each too small for the 7 Gbps the organization uses.
A 100 Gbps primary connection greatly overprovisions and adds significant cost for links and network devices.
source: CompTIA Security+ Practice Tests: Exam SY0-701 (Seidl) – Chapter 3: Domain 3.0: Security Architecture, Review Questions question 157

stem: Jaime is concerned about the volume of logs that her new application may create. What capacity planning item should she focus on?
explanation: Large volumes of logs need space, so storage capacity should be part of Jaime's infrastructure planning. Planning for it keeps the logs from overwhelming her infrastructure.
whyWrong: Compute is not usually an issue for collecting logs, although it may be for analyzing them later.
Power is not directly affected by the volume of logs.
People are not directly affected by logging, although analysts may be needed later.
source: CompTIA Security+ Practice Tests: Exam SY0-701 (Seidl) – Chapter 3: Domain 3.0: Security Architecture, Review Questions question 184

stem: Alaina is planning how to staff her warm site in the case of a natural disaster that disables her primary site. What concern is most likely to impact her capacity planning for staff in this scenario?
options: Whether staff will be able to reach the site
Whether staff will be impacted by the disaster
Whether the site will be impacted by the disaster
Whether generator fuel will be available
explanation: Capacity planning for disaster operations must account for the effect of the disaster on the staff themselves. Staff may have no power, Internet access, or even housing, so they may not be available to work.
whyWrong: Many operations can be run remotely, so reaching the site is less of a concern than whether staff are available at all.
Whether the site itself is affected is a site resilience issue, not staff capacity planning.
Generator fuel is a power and facility concern, not staff capacity planning.
source: CompTIA Security+ Practice Tests: Exam SY0-701 (Seidl) – Chapter 3: Domain 3.0: Security Architecture, Review Questions question 88

stem: Which of the following is a common part of technology capacity planning for resilience?
explanation: Load balancers are a common part of technology capacity planning for resilience. They spread traffic across clustered applications and servers, so the service continues if one server fails.
whyWrong: Cross-training staff is a people capacity planning measure.
Geographically diverse datacenters are an infrastructure resilience option.
Uninterruptible power supplies are an infrastructure resilience option.
source: CompTIA Security+ Practice Tests: Exam SY0-701 (Seidl) – Chapter 3: Domain 3.0: Security Architecture, Review Questions question 92

stem: WebServ Corp., a web hosting company, has been analyzing the reliability of its servers. They found that one of their server models, on average, tends to fail once every 2000 hours and then gets promptly repaired. Which of the following metrics is WebServ Corp. evaluating?
explanation: Mean time between failures (MTBF) measures how reliable hardware or a system is. It is the average time from one failure to the next, so a server model that fails about every 2000 hours has an MTBF of 2000 hours.
whyWrong: RTO is the target time to restore a business process after an interruption, not the time between failures.
MTTR is the average time needed to repair a failed component, not the time between failures.
RPO is the maximum acceptable data loss measured in time, not a reliability measure.
source: CompTIA Security+ SY0-701 Practice Tests & PBQs (Gorgotsias) – Chapter 5: Security Program Management and Oversight, Practice Questions question 10

stem: After a recent security breach, CyberSolutions Inc. evaluated their response metrics and determined that, on average, it took 4 hours from identifying a security breach to having it completely resolved. Which metric best describes this 4-hour timeframe?
explanation: Mean time to repair (MTTR) is the average time needed to repair a failed component or system and return it to operation. The average of 4 hours from identifying a breach to resolving it is CyberSolutions' MTTR for breaches.
whyWrong: RTO is a target set in advance for restoring a process, not a measured average.
RPO is the maximum acceptable data loss measured in time.
MTBF is the expected time between failures during normal operation.
source: CompTIA Security+ SY0-701 Practice Tests & PBQs (Gorgotsias) – Chapter 5: Security Program Management and Oversight, Practice Questions question 16
note: MTTR is defined for repairs of failed components; the book applies it loosely to the average time to resolve a breach.

stem: AcmeBank recently performed a business impact analysis for its online banking system. The result indicated that the bank could tolerate a maximum downtime of 4 hours for the system before incurring significant financial losses and customer dissatisfaction. Which concept best describes this 4-hour period?
explanation: Maximum tolerable downtime (MTD) is the longest time a business process can be down before the organization suffers unacceptable harm. A business impact analysis that finds the bank can tolerate at most 4 hours of downtime before significant losses has found the MTD, and the RTO is then set at or below it.
whyWrong: RPO is the maximum acceptable data loss measured in time, not a period of downtime.
RTO is the target time for restoring the system, which the organization sets within the maximum tolerable downtime.
Time to restore measures how long a restoration actually takes, not how much downtime the business can tolerate.
source: CompTIA Security+ SY0-701 Practice Tests & PBQs (Gorgotsias) – Chapter 5: Security Program Management and Oversight, Practice Questions question 36
note: Book key: C (RTO); corrected to B (MTD) because the 4 hours is the maximum downtime the business can tolerate, and the RTO is the recovery target set within it. Explanation rewritten. MTD is not named in SY0-801 3.4 recovery metrics.

stem: WebFlix, a popular online movie streaming service, experienced a data center outage due to a natural disaster. They had backups in place and restored their systems using data from 6 hours prior to the outage. This resulted in the loss of some user interactions, like ratings and watchlists from the last 6 hours. What term describes the 6-hour gap between the last backup and the time of the outage?
explanation: The recovery point objective (RPO) is the maximum acceptable amount of data loss, measured in time back from the incident. WebFlix restored data from 6 hours before the outage, so its recovery point gap was 6 hours of lost user activity.
whyWrong: RTO is the maximum acceptable time a system can be down, not the amount of data lost.
MTD is the total time a system can be non-operational before significant losses, not the data lost.
Recovery Duration Period is not a standard business continuity term.
source: CompTIA Security+ SY0-701 Practice Tests & PBQs (Gorgotsias) – Chapter 5: Security Program Management and Oversight, Practice Questions question 48

stem: How is mean time between failures (MTBF) used in designing a robust disaster recovery plan (DRP)?
options: In determining the average repair time for failed devices or systems
In predicting the cost and time needed for regular system maintenance
In anticipating the frequency of potential failures and planning for system resilience
In calculating the total downtime experienced during an outage
explanation: Mean time between failures (MTBF) is the expected average time between failures of a system or component. In a disaster recovery plan it helps anticipate how often failures may happen, so systems can be designed with redundancy to withstand them.
whyWrong: The average repair time for failed systems is the mean time to repair (MTTR).
MTBF predicts how often failures happen, not the cost and time of regular maintenance.
Total downtime during an outage depends on repair and recovery time, not on MTBF.
source: CompTIA Security+ SY0-701 Cert Guide (Heuermann) – Chapter 24: Understanding Elements of the Risk Management Process, Do I Know This Already? Quiz question 10
note: The book quiz has no key; answer written from the chapter.

stem: What is the primary purpose of calculating mean time to repair (MTTR) in a disaster recovery plan (DRP)?
options: To determine the cost-effectiveness of spare parts stockpiles
To understand the operational impact of repair times and guide decision making for redundancy
To predict when a system failure might occur
To calculate the number of failures per billion hours of operation
explanation: Mean time to repair (MTTR) is the average time needed to repair a failed device or system and return it to operation. In a disaster recovery plan it shows the operational impact of repair times and guides decisions about redundancy or keeping spare parts.
whyWrong: Spare parts are one possible outcome of the decision, but MTTR's purpose is to understand the impact of repair times.
Predicting how often failures may occur is the purpose of mean time between failures (MTBF).
The number of failures per billion hours of operation is the failure in time (FIT) metric.
source: CompTIA Security+ SY0-701 Cert Guide (Heuermann) – Chapter 24: Understanding Elements of the Risk Management Process, Do I Know This Already? Quiz question 9
note: The book quiz has no key; answer written from the chapter.

stem: In business impact analysis, which component is crucial for determining the acceptable data loss and downtime in IT systems?
options: Recovery point objective and recovery time objective
explanation: The recovery point objective (RPO) and recovery time objective (RTO) set the acceptable data loss and downtime in a business impact analysis. RPO is the acceptable data loss measured in time, and RTO is the acceptable time a service or system can be down.
whyWrong: MTBF measures a system's reliability and does not set acceptable data loss or downtime.
Data frequency analysis is not a standard business impact analysis term.
Impact acceptance threshold is not a recognized business impact analysis concept.
source: CompTIA Security+ SY0-701 Certification Guide, 3rd edition (Neil) – Chapter 24: Explain elements of the risk management process, Chapter Review Questions question 10

stem: Which statement BEST describes the critical difference between recovery time objective and recovery point objective within the context of business impact analysis?
options: Recovery time objective refers to the maximum allowable downtime, while recovery point objective refers to the maximum allowable data loss.
Recovery time objective refers to the frequency of system failures, while recovery point objective refers to the maximum allowable downtime.
Recovery time objective refers to the maximum allowable data loss, while recovery point objective refers to the maximum allowable downtime.
Recovery time objective and recovery point objective both refer to the maximum allowable downtime but are used in different contexts.
explanation: The recovery time objective (RTO) is the maximum length of time a service or system can be down after an incident before the impact on the business is unacceptable. The recovery point objective (RPO) is the maximum acceptable data loss, measured as the age of the data that must be recovered from backup.
whyWrong: The frequency of system failures is described by MTBF, not RTO, and RPO concerns data loss rather than downtime.
This statement switches the definitions of RTO and RPO.
RTO and RPO have different definitions, and only RTO concerns downtime.
source: CompTIA Security+ SY0-701 Certification Guide, 3rd edition (Neil) – Chapter 24: Explain elements of the risk management process, Chapter Review Questions question 9

stem: Nancy wants to adopt a backup strategy that will meet her organization’s desires about the amount of data that could be lost in a scenario where a restoration from backup was required and also wants to establish guidelines for how long a restoration should take. What two key objectives should she set?
explanation: A recovery point objective (RPO) describes how much data it is acceptable to lose, and a recovery time objective (RTO) describes the maximum time a recovery should take. Together they guide backup strategy and infrastructure design.
whyWrong: RFBT is not a real recovery metric.
MTBF describes the average time between device failures, not how long a restoration should take.
MTBF is a reliability measure and RFBT is not a real metric.
source: CompTIA Security+ Practice Tests: Exam SY0-701 (Seidl) – Chapter 3: Domain 3.0: Security Architecture, Review Questions question 1

stem: Barb’s organization has a recovery point objective of 6 hours. At least how often should Barb conduct incremental backups to meet this RPO?
explanation: A 6-hour RPO means that no more than 6 hours of data may be lost, so Barb must back up at least once every 6 hours. She might run backups slightly more often to make sure the RPO is always met.
whyWrong: Hourly backups far exceed the target and may affect performance and recovery time, so they are more often than required.
Backups every 12 hours could lose up to 12 hours of data, which misses the 6-hour RPO.
Daily backups could lose up to a day of data, which misses the 6-hour RPO.
source: CompTIA Security+ Practice Tests: Exam SY0-701 (Seidl) – Chapter 3: Domain 3.0: Security Architecture, Review Questions question 123

stem: Olivia’s organization operates servers in a datacenter that support customers across the country. As Olivia is determining her service level agreements, what information is most important in determining how quickly a server can be restored to operation if its motherboard fails?
explanation: Mean time to repair (MTTR) is the average time it takes to repair a system or device, such as replacing a failed motherboard. Olivia needs it to know what she can promise in service level agreements that depend on server repair times.
whyWrong: An RTO is a restoration goal that must take repair time into account; it does not tell how fast a server can be fixed.
An RPO describes how much data can be lost, not how fast a server can be repaired.
MTBF measures how often failures happen, not how long a repair takes.
source: CompTIA Security+ Practice Tests: Exam SY0-701 (Seidl) – Chapter 5: Domain 5.0: Security Program Management and Oversight, Review Questions question 102

stem: Dani’s organization relies on journaling to help protect transactions that occur through its database. Which of the following does journaling impact the most?
explanation: The recovery point objective (RPO) describes how much data can be lost in an outage. Journaling lets transactions be replayed against the restored database, so it most affects how little data is lost.
whyWrong: Journaling may slow recovery because transactions are replayed, but its main effect is on data loss rather than the RTO.
MTTR is the average time to repair a system or device and is not what journaling protects.
MTBF measures a system's reliability and is not affected by journaling.
source: CompTIA Security+ Practice Tests: Exam SY0-701 (Seidl) – Chapter 5: Domain 5.0: Security Program Management and Oversight, Review Questions question 104

stem: Henry’s organization has set their RTO to 12 hours. What does this mean?
options: Outages must be less than 6 hours long.
Recovery from outages should take less than 12 hours.
Outages longer than 12 hours will require fail over to a warm site.
SLAs for third-party services should specify a 12 hour MTBF.
explanation: A recovery time objective (RTO) states how long restoring systems or services to normal function after a disruption may take. A 12-hour RTO means that recovery from outages should take less than 12 hours.
whyWrong: A 12-hour RTO does not set a 6-hour limit on outages.
Starting a failover to a warm site only after 12 hours would miss the 12-hour RTO.
MTBF is the mean time between failures, not a recovery timeframe.
source: CompTIA Security+ Practice Tests: Exam SY0-701 (Seidl) – Chapter 5: Domain 5.0: Security Program Management and Oversight, Review Questions question 105

stem: Valerie knows that her organization’s datacenter power infrastructure has an MTTR of 24 hours. What should she do if there is a critical component failure in her power infrastructure, and the organization has a warm site with an activation of 12 hours and needs to be back online as soon as possible?
options: Wait to see if the recovery can be done in less than 24 hours.
Immediately begin a move to the warm site.
Wait to see if the recovery can be done in less than 12 hours.
Wait for 12 hours, then begin the move to the warm site.
explanation: Valerie should immediately begin a move to the warm site, because activating it takes 12 hours, half of the 24-hour average repair time. In most cases moving will shorten the outage by about 12 hours, and if the repair finishes sooner she can stop the move.
whyWrong: Waiting for the repair means an average outage of 24 hours, twice the time needed to activate the warm site.
Waiting 12 hours before deciding uses up the time in which the warm site could already have been activated.
Starting the move after 12 hours means an outage of about 24 hours, no shorter than waiting for the repair.
source: CompTIA Security+ Practice Tests: Exam SY0-701 (Seidl) – Chapter 5: Domain 5.0: Security Program Management and Oversight, Review Questions question 106

stem: A security administrator is reviewing the company’s continuity plan, and it specifies an RTO of four hours and an RPO of one day. Which of the following is the plan describing?
options: Systems should be restored within one day and should remain operational for at least four hours.
Systems should be restored within four hours and no later than one day after the incident.
Systems should be restored within one day and lose, at most, four hours’ worth of data.
Systems should be restored within four hours with a loss of one day’s worth of data at most.
explanation: The recovery time objective (RTO) is the time within which a service must be restored after a disruption, and the recovery point objective (RPO) is the maximum acceptable data loss measured in time. An RTO of four hours and an RPO of one day mean that systems are restored within four hours and lose at most one day of data.
whyWrong: The RTO is four hours, not one day, and neither metric says how long systems must stay operational.
The RPO describes data loss, not a second restoration deadline.
This statement switches the RTO and RPO values.
source: CompTIA Security+ Practice Tests: Exam SY0-701 (Seidl) – Chapter 5: Domain 5.0: Security Program Management and Oversight, Review Questions question 140
note: The book explanation said "minimum loss"; rewritten as a loss of at most one day of data.

stem: You are a server administrator for your company’s private cloud. To provide service to employees, you are instructed to use reliable hard disks in the server to host a virtual environment. Which of the following best describes the reliability of hard drives?
explanation: Mean time between failures (MTBF) measures the reliability of a system or component. It is the expected time that passes between failures, so a higher MTBF means a more reliable hard disk.
whyWrong: MTTR is the average time to repair or replace a failed component, not a measure of reliability.
An RPO is the amount of data, measured in time, that a company can tolerate losing.
ALE is the annual loss expectancy, the product of the annual rate of occurrence and the single loss expectancy.
source: CompTIA Security+ Practice Tests: Exam SY0-701 (Seidl) – Chapter 5: Domain 5.0: Security Program Management and Oversight, Review Questions question 144

stem: Which of the following concepts defines a company goal for system restoration and acceptable data loss?
explanation: The recovery point objective (RPO) is a goal the company sets for the data loss it can accept when it restores systems. It is the amount of time during an interruption before the data lost exceeds the maximum the business continuity plan accepts.
whyWrong: MTBF is a rating that predicts the expected time between failures of a device, not a recovery goal.
MTTR is the average time to repair or replace a failed device or component, not a goal for acceptable data loss.
ARO is the annual rate of occurrence, an estimate of how often a threat will occur in a year.
source: CompTIA Security+ Practice Tests: Exam SY0-701 (Seidl) – Chapter 5: Domain 5.0: Security Program Management and Oversight, Review Questions question 149

stem: Which of the following terms is used to measure how maintainable a system or device is?
explanation: Mean time to repair (MTTR) is the average time it takes to repair a system or device after a failure, so it measures how maintainable the system is. It is calculated by dividing the total maintenance time by the number of repairs, and it helps decide whether a system needs more redundancy.
whyWrong: MTBF measures reliability as the time between failures, not maintainability.
MTTF is the mean time to failure, a reliability measure for devices that are not repaired.
MITM is an on-path attack, not a measure of maintainability.
source: CompTIA Security+ Practice Tests: Exam SY0-701 (Seidl) – Chapter 5: Domain 5.0: Security Program Management and Oversight, Review Questions question 153

stem: What measure is used to describe the average functional lifespan of a device in use?
explanation: Mean time between failures (MTBF) describes the average time before a device fails, or the average time between failures of a system. It is used to estimate how long a device will function in use.
whyWrong: An RTO is the time an organization allows for restoring systems or services after a disruption.
MTTR is the average time it takes to repair a system or device.
An RPO describes how much data can be lost in an outage.
source: CompTIA Security+ Practice Tests: Exam SY0-701 (Seidl) – Chapter 5: Domain 5.0: Security Program Management and Oversight, Review Questions question 209

stem: Jill’s organization wants to ensure that services and systems are back online and functioning normally within 4 hours of an event or incident. What term best describes this goal?
explanation: A recovery time objective (RTO) is the goal an organization sets for how long restoring systems or services to normal function after a disruption can take. A goal of being back online within 4 hours is an RTO.
whyWrong: MTTR is the measured average time to repair a system or device, not a restoration goal.
An RPO describes how much data can be lost in an outage.
MTBF measures reliability as the expected time between failures.
source: CompTIA Security+ Practice Tests: Exam SY0-701 (Seidl) – Chapter 5: Domain 5.0: Security Program Management and Oversight, Review Questions question 3

stem: Jack’s organization recently received a shipment of SSDs and has begun to deploy them. What information would best help Jack assess the useful life of the devices?
explanation: The manufacturer's published mean time between failures (MTBF) measures reliability as the expected time between failures. Knowing how long devices should last on average helps Jack assess their useful life and plan budgets, even though devices are often replaced before then.
whyWrong: An RTO is the time allowed for restoring systems or services after a disruption.
MTTR is the average time it takes to repair a system or device.
An RPO describes how much data can be lost in an outage.
source: CompTIA Security+ Practice Tests: Exam SY0-701 (Seidl) – Chapter 5: Domain 5.0: Security Program Management and Oversight, Review Questions question 97

stem: The hard drives that Jason’s organization recently purchased have an MTBF of 300,000 hours. When can Jason expect the first drive to fail?
explanation: Mean time between failures (MTBF) is only an average across many devices, not a prediction for any single drive. Individual drives can fail well before or after 300,000 hours, so Jason cannot know when the first one will fail.
whyWrong: Half the MTBF is not a predicted failure point, because MTBF is only an average.
MTBF is an average across many drives, not the time at which a given drive will fail.
Drives can fail at any time, and nothing makes 450,000 hours a predicted failure point.
source: CompTIA Security+ Practice Tests: Exam SY0-701 (Seidl) – Chapter 5: Domain 5.0: Security Program Management and Oversight, Review Questions question 98
note: The book explanation said half of the drives fail before the MTBF; rewritten, because MTBF is an average and does not predict when a single drive fails.

stem: Melissa’s organization wants to establish a metric that defines how much data could be lost if an issue occurs. What should they set?
explanation: A recovery point objective (RPO) describes how much data can be lost if an outage or other issue occurs. It is the metric an organization sets to define acceptable data loss.
whyWrong: An RTO describes how long restoring systems or services after a disruption can take.
MTTR is the average time it takes to repair a system or device.
MTBF measures reliability as the expected time between failures.
source: CompTIA Security+ Practice Tests: Exam SY0-701 (Seidl) – Chapter 5: Domain 5.0: Security Program Management and Oversight, Review Questions question 99
